category_title: Reluctant communicators who avoid using communication aids and struggle to make choices
minimal_context: Lily is participating in a group story-making activity in the sensory room and is asked to use her communication book to suggest ideas for the drama.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Lily, it is time for our story-making activity in the spinney. What should happen next in our drama? Please use your communication book to show me your idea.

STUDENT: (Looks away from the communication book and keeps her hands in her lap, reluctant to use the aid when asked the direct question.)

TUTOR: What do you think? Just point to something in the book.

STUDENT: No. (Frowns and uses a sad facial expression, refusing to sign or point.)

TUTOR: We need you to suggest an idea for the story. Keep trying.

STUDENT: (Looks visibly cross and pushes the communication book away, remaining completely reluctant to suggest any ideas or make a choice for the story.)

options.A: Provide an anchored experience through a class visit to a local spinney and take photos to use as visual prompts on a smartboard and iPad.
options.B: Use Evernote on the iPad to take notes, organize their story ideas, and archive past drama projects during the classroom literacy project.
options.C: Encourage students to assume leadership roles in the story-making activity (lead director, lead script editor, lead creative designer) and enable groups to assign these themselves.
options.D: Apply increasingly serious disciplinary measures, such as classroom suspension, detention, and school suspension, if the reluctance to participate continues during the story-making activity.
